  Dev-memory (5):
    - fa1777b guard-bypass/project: A/B measurement of B-cee5 prompt stopgap: agents deviate from scan mandates either way, and no mechanical read-evidence exists to detect it.
      lesson: Old full-scan prompt: the agent silently disobeyed (read 1 of 111 decisions docs, no audit trail) yet asserted complete coverage — in production such deviation is invisible, so coverage claims under the old prompt were unverifiable; when agents DO obey, the 2.4MB corpus costs ~600k+ input tokens (the original exhaustion). New bounded contract produced equivalent review quality (same load-bearing gaps and same spec-contradiction OQ) at 74.8k vs 79.3k tokens with a recorded enumeration + candidate basis + explicit non-escalation reason. Core gap remaining: what a reviewer actually READ is self-reported prose, not evidence — there is no read manifest bound to scope_check_save/review_pass_set and no transcript-derived read log, so future before/after comparisons and compliance proofs (detecting unrecorded full scans) have no ground truth. Prompt-layer stopgap is instructional only; proof needs mechanical read evidence.
      reuse: reviewer read evidence, scan compliance, token stopgap measurement, read manifest, scanEscalationReason audit, B-cee5 effect
    - e5bcf07 failure-mode/project: A story whose diff includes package.json turns every later main merge into related drift: quorum, delivery-check, and review passes all stale and force a full re-review round.
      lesson: storyFilesHash covers the story diff file set. package.json is in that set whenever the story wires npm scripts (or gets scope-acknowledged version bumps), and DONE auto-bumps touch package.json on every merge to main — so any sibling story landing first changes YOUR story-owned material. Cost in B-3b05: one extra TEST->DEV->REVIEW round (4 reviewer lanes re-pass), fresh quorum_submit, fresh delivery_check_set. Mitigations: close stories promptly once quorum is bound; expect and budget the round-4 re-review when parallel stories share package.json; command-backed evidence must be actually re-run (refresh_stale refuses to rebind it silently).
      reuse: stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch after merge / review assurance floor local rounds 0 after mergeMain / related drift package.json
    - ca4455e workflow/project: Run quorum_submit during REVIEW, before advancing to TEST, once all active lanes have current-round passes.
      lesson: quorum_submit satisfies the 3x2 review-assurance floor by converting CURRENT-round signed review passes from ALL active reviewer lanes into host verdict records (hostA=claude-cli hostB=codex-cli); it refuses to fabricate. review_run_start/review_pass_set are REVIEW-phase-only, so advancing to TEST first (the round-2+ gate needs only >=1 receipt) strands the other lanes without a write path and forces a TEST->DEV->REVIEW round-trip to mint fresh passes in a new round. Correct order: all lanes pass in current round -> quorum_submit -> story_advance TEST.
      reuse: review assurance floor blocked / quorum_submit missing current pass lanes / review_pass_set not available in TEST
    - 9bd6b5a workflow/project: Default 3x2 host verification uses codex-cli and claude-cli; agy-cli is fallback only.
      lesson: Use codex-cli and claude-cli as the primary independent hosts. Use agy-cli only when Claude CLI or Codex CLI is unavailable, quota-limited, or an explicit standby/substitute host is needed. This supersedes dev-memory d6f173d, which described agy-cli as fallback mainly for Claude.
      reuse: host verification policy codex claude agy fallback unavailable quota

name: code-review
description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point — a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here — not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below — a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation — and, like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name** — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code** — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy** — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps** — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession** — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches** — the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery** — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change** — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality** — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains** — long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man** — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest** — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

**Standards sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full — the sub-agent has no other access to it.
- The brief: "Report — per file/hunk where relevant — (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings — the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes — that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

On 2026-08-13 the user confirmed that the failure occurs when one provider host launches another provider through CLI mode, such as Claude invoking Codex or Codex invoking Claude. A ten-minute caller timeout can detach or terminate observation even though the provider process may still be doing useful work. The related B-1be5 proposal only considered heuristic ledger provenance and does not solve this execution failure. During B-137a PLAN scope review, the first design was formally reopened because its evidence write ordering would either deadlock before terminal or let the controller impersonate the reviewer.

## Key Insights

The framework must supervise the provider process at the actual execution boundary. A worker heartbeat and provider progress are different facts; output silence is diagnostic rather than terminal. Every wait must be bounded, every run must have a finite absolute deadline, and a durable next-touch reconciler must be able to materialize terminal truth even when the original worker becomes wedged. Formal reviewer evidence must bind to the exact managed receipt instead of provider plus story plus time-window guesses.

Reviewer evidence also needs a two-phase provenance protocol. The provider reviewer authors an immutable proposal containing its pass/findings and truthful read evidence while the run is active. It cannot call the final evidence writer before the terminal receipt and evidence journal are sealed. After successful terminal, a mechanical importer validates the sealed proposal and imports it without allowing the controller to change the verdict or become the reviewer. The new composite evidence class must use the existing shared Proof Admissibility artifact registry, intake, reason vocabulary and evaluator at both write-time and REVIEW-gate consumption; a parallel special-case proof system is not acceptable.

## Solution Tradeoffs

A single deep ManagedHostRun module adds durable runtime artifacts, worker continuation and reconciliation complexity, but removes duplicated foreground/background supervision and makes cancellation, cleanup and evidence semantics consistent. M1 execution safety and M2 gate evidence ship together so the framework does not claim enforcement while raw CLI reviews can still satisfy formal gates. The two-phase proposal/import protocol adds one post-terminal mechanical step, but preserves the actual provider reviewer as evidence author and prevents controller self-absolution. Reusing shared Proof Admissibility adds registry work but avoids a second trust vocabulary and keeps gate-consumed facts centrally auditable. Legacy configured provider timeout ceilings remain separate and unchanged.

## Conversational Texture

The user repeatedly emphasized that a ten-minute boundary must not cause an automatic restart, that silent but still-running agents should continue to be monitored, and that the target is host-independent cross-provider CLI execution rather than native subagent APIs. After iterative Claude Opus review and empirical Codex/POSIX probes, the user approved the consolidated design and explicitly asked to start a Story and implement it. The user values a framework-level solution at the provider CLI boundary: bounded observation, no duplicate restart, honest terminal/cancel truth, and proof that the exact provider review—not a controller-authored substitute—satisfied the formal gate.
# B-137a implementation plan

## Public seams and invariant order

The behavior-facing seams are:
1. `host_run` submit/foreground attach;
2. `host_run_status(runId, waitMs<=30000)`;
3. `host_run_cancel(runId, reason?)`;
4. `cross_host_review` as the privileged verdict-profile owner;
5. `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` plus the REVIEW gate as managed-evidence consumers.

Private worker, file layout, launch adapters and reconciliation helpers are tested only through those seams or through real child-process effects. Each vertical slice follows RED → minimal GREEN; implementation does not bulk-create imagined internal tests.

## CHK-001 — Persist and reconcile managed host-run lifecycle

Create a deep `core/managed-host-run.ts` module whose small interface owns submit, attach/status projection, cancel, worker execution and reconcile. A run gets a generated `hrun_*` identity and an immutable root under `.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`.

Submit writes immutable/spec-bound state atomically: `spec.json`, digest-only `owner.json`, 0600 one-shot `input.cap` and `input.prompt`, initial `snapshot.json`, and append-only `events.jsonl`. The hidden worker wins `claim.json` using exclusive create, validates the one-shot capability, unlinks both input files, marks `claimReady`, acquires provider admission, launches the private provider adapter and periodically advances `workerHeartbeatAt`. Provider output updates a separate `lastProviderProgressAt` only when observable; unsupported observability is represented as `unobservable`, never fabricated.

A terminal is created exclusively and exactly once. It records outcome, timing, exit/timeout/cancel reason, provider identity, spec/profile binding digests, evidence journal digest, process cleanup facts, residual process state and an independent `replacementSafe`. Repeated status/cancel/attach calls first acquire a short `reconcile.lock`, re-read facts, and materialize terminal truth for deadline expiry or authoritative worker/provider death. Silence is never a transition predicate. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity yields honest residual `unknown` and `replacementSafe:false`, not blind termination.

Initial RED tests cover: exclusive claim winner, unchanged running state across silent intervals, worker crash followed by deadline reconciliation, one terminal under concurrent reconcilers, idempotent status/cancel, terminal/result digest stability, capability/prompt deletion, and no automatic retry.

## CHK-002 — Expose submit, attach, status and cancel command surfaces

Extend the host-run command schema:
- `host_run --detach` submits, waits only for a bounded claim handshake, and returns `runId/state/deadlineAt/generation`;
- foreground `host_run` calls the same submit path then attaches to that run, projecting live output and final usage without owning the provider child;
- `host_run_status --runId ... --waitMs ...` performs bounded long-poll, returning immediately on terminal or snapshot-generation change and otherwise after at most 30000ms;
- `host_run_cancel --runId ... --reason ...` writes an idempotent cooperative request and reconciles;
- hidden `host_run_worker --runId ...` is runtime-only and never advertised as an operator workflow.

Declare command policy, process-fact level and CLI watchdog behavior for runtime continuation. A foreground caller/watchdog exit may end attachment but cannot convert the managed run to failed or cancel the worker. JSON stdout remains one machine object; text mode keeps live stream routing and concise status guidance. The handler never stores raw prompt/capability in argv or durable public artifacts.

RED starts at CLI/handler seams: detach returns after claim, status wait is capped, foreground and detached share one run/receipt shape, cancel is idempotent, unknown run is fail-closed, and caller termination leaves the run queryable.

## CHK-003 — Supervise provider processes portably and honestly

Provider adapters remain private to ManagedHostRun and preserve canonical launcher specifications. Codex uses documented `codex exec ... -`, the worker writes the prompt to stdin and closes it. Claude retains its canonical launcher contract. Agy is unavailable for ManagedHostRun because its current print launcher accepts the prompt only in argv, so managed execution refuses it before provider spawn until a stdin or protected prompt-file transport exists.

On POSIX, spawn the provider as a new process group and persist PID/PGID plus a launch fingerprint. Cancellation/deadline cleanup is TERM → bounded grace → KILL → reap → residual probe. Identity is revalidated before signals. On unsupported platforms, managed execution refuses before provider spawn with a structured unsupported-platform terminal; it does not silently degrade to child-only cleanup.

Move the first-output clock to diagnostics only. Preserve finite total timeout/deadline, bounded output projection, provider usage candidate extraction, turn-failure diagnostic, passthrough-degradation honesty and failure classification. Worker heartbeat and provider progress are distinct fields.

RED uses real local Node subprocesses for silent completion, descendant cleanup and TERM-resistant escalation, plus injected provider adapters for Codex argv/stdin closure, overflow and parsing.

## CHK-004 — Enforce shared provider admission independent of usage-ledger mode

Extract the slot registry from the ledger-gated branch into one provider-admission module. Acquisition happens before every provider spawn regardless of `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER`; usage preflight/budget/final rows remain conditional and keep existing fail-closed/append-honesty semantics. Slot ownership token, dead-PID reclaim, corrupt-meta stale backstop and token-guarded release remain unchanged.

Inventory production provider launch sites. Managed host_run and cross_host_review use ManagedHostRun admission. Direct Codex/Claude/Gemini leaves that are not managed execution are classified by the provider execution registry as `admission_only` or `adapter_only` according to their admission owner; `legacy_unmanaged` is reserved and empty by contract, and `admission_managed` is not a status. Add a source registry/contract smoke so a new direct spawn path fails review until classified.

Preserve candidate-spec per-chunk streaming, 64KiB discard-all overflow and null first-output diagnostics. RED covers ledger-off cap contention, dead/corrupt/live slot reclaim, release race, and source inventory completeness.

## CHK-005 — Route cross-host review through managed execution

Keep `cross_host_review` as profile owner. It still resolves the authoritative story worktree, captures clean HEAD/material/storyFiles facts, authorizes read-only Codex dispatch, creates the detached review snapshot, redacts environment, computes the existing policy timeout ceiling, constructs the structured-verdict prompt and validates the returned verdict schema.

Replace only its direct provider execution with internal ManagedHostRun submit+attach using profile `cross-host-verdict` and opaque bindings. The terminal receipt is included in paired host-verdict provenance. Provider nonzero/timeout/cancel/admission refusal/invalid verdict continue to yield the existing honest blocked/error decision; no raw provider stdout becomes gate evidence.

Protect configured `provider.codex`, `cross_host_review`, bounded retry and fail-closed policies with exact source/runtime regression assertions. RED captures the current direct leaf, then proves the managed path while all existing cross-host checks remain green.

## CHK-006 — Bind formal reviewer evidence to exact managed receipts

Add a versioned managed-execution binding and a two-phase provider-authored evidence protocol. The profile owner seals opaque bindings at submit: storyId, reviewRunId, lane, intended provider/transport, prompt-envelope/body/context/assembled digests, materialHash, headHash and storyFilesHash. While running, the provider reviewer writes exactly one immutable proposal into the evidence journal: pass or findings plus truthful readManifest/readLog and its registered reviewer identity. It does not call final `review_pass_set` or `finding_add`.

Successful terminal creation seals the spec digest, proposal digest and append-only journal digest. After terminal, `managed_review_evidence_import` accepts only a runId/receipt reference, reads the sealed provider-authored bytes, and imports the existing ReviewPass/Finding shape while preserving agent/lane/reviewRun/read provenance exactly. It exposes no verdict/note/finding override fields, is idempotent, and refuses non-success terminal, residual/replacement ambiguity, missing/multiple proposals or any digest mismatch. The controller may trigger import but cannot become the reviewer or reinterpret its verdict.

Register this managed receipt/composite evidence as a canonical artifact kind in shared Proof Admissibility with producer boundary, scope, REVIEW consumer, claim kind, temporal/material role, semantic field binding and canonical reason codes. Both import-time admission and the REVIEW gate must call the same shared registry/intake/evaluator; process-fact registry declares the gate semantics but is not a substitute. The gate revalidates current terminal, proposal/journal integrity, exact ReviewRun/lane/provider/prompt envelope and current material tuple instead of trusting persisted booleans.

Native-host reviewer lanes retain their existing signed ReviewRun/pass/finding path and are not falsely described as mechanically supervised by ManagedHostRun. Main/implementer/controller-authored evidence, raw CLI output, usage-ledger rows, B-1be5-style time-window matching, pre-terminal proposals and structured degraded decisions cannot upgrade to normal managed receipt assurance.

RED tests the valid provider proposal → successful terminal seal → importer → REVIEW gate path, plus forged runId/terminal/journal/proposal, stale/cross-story/cross-lane/cross-provider/material mismatch, raw CLI absence, controller override/self-assertion, multiple proposals, importer replay, and non-success terminal. A mutation/source-contract test proves both write-time and gate call the shared evaluator: bypassing either call or adding a parallel special-case evaluator must fail.

On 2026-08-13 the user confirmed that the failure occurs when one provider host launches another provider through CLI mode, such as Claude invoking Codex or Codex invoking Claude. A ten-minute caller timeout can detach or terminate observation even though the provider process may still be doing useful work. The related B-1be5 proposal only considered heuristic ledger provenance and does not solve this execution failure. During B-137a PLAN scope review, the first design was formally reopened because its evidence write ordering would either deadlock before terminal or let the controller impersonate the reviewer.

## Key Insights

The framework must supervise the provider process at the actual execution boundary. A worker heartbeat and provider progress are different facts; output silence is diagnostic rather than terminal. Every wait must be bounded, every run must have a finite absolute deadline, and a durable next-touch reconciler must be able to materialize terminal truth even when the original worker becomes wedged. Formal reviewer evidence must bind to the exact managed receipt instead of provider plus story plus time-window guesses.

Reviewer evidence also needs a two-phase provenance protocol. The provider reviewer authors an immutable proposal containing its pass/findings and truthful read evidence while the run is active. It cannot call the final evidence writer before the terminal receipt and evidence journal are sealed. After successful terminal, a mechanical importer validates the sealed proposal and imports it without allowing the controller to change the verdict or become the reviewer. The new composite evidence class must use the existing shared Proof Admissibility artifact registry, intake, reason vocabulary and evaluator at both write-time and REVIEW-gate consumption; a parallel special-case proof system is not acceptable.

## Solution Tradeoffs

A single deep ManagedHostRun module adds durable runtime artifacts, worker continuation and reconciliation complexity, but removes duplicated foreground/background supervision and makes cancellation, cleanup and evidence semantics consistent. M1 execution safety and M2 gate evidence ship together so the framework does not claim enforcement while raw CLI reviews can still satisfy formal gates. The two-phase proposal/import protocol adds one post-terminal mechanical step, but preserves the actual provider reviewer as evidence author and prevents controller self-absolution. Reusing shared Proof Admissibility adds registry work but avoids a second trust vocabulary and keeps gate-consumed facts centrally auditable. Legacy configured provider timeout ceilings remain separate and unchanged.

## Conversational Texture

The user repeatedly emphasized that a ten-minute boundary must not cause an automatic restart, that silent but still-running agents should continue to be monitored, and that the target is host-independent cross-provider CLI execution rather than native subagent APIs. After iterative Claude Opus review and empirical Codex/POSIX probes, the user approved the consolidated design and explicitly asked to start a Story and implement it. The user values a framework-level solution at the provider CLI boundary: bounded observation, no duplicate restart, honest terminal/cancel truth, and proof that the exact provider review—not a controller-authored substitute—satisfied the formal gate.
# B-137a implementation plan

## Public seams and invariant order

The behavior-facing seams are:
1. `host_run` submit/foreground attach;
2. `host_run_status(runId, waitMs<=30000)`;
3. `host_run_cancel(runId, reason?)`;
4. `cross_host_review` as the privileged verdict-profile owner;
5. `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` plus the REVIEW gate as managed-evidence consumers.

Private worker, file layout, launch adapters and reconciliation helpers are tested only through those seams or through real child-process effects. Each vertical slice follows RED → minimal GREEN; implementation does not bulk-create imagined internal tests.

## CHK-001 — Persist and reconcile managed host-run lifecycle

Create a deep `core/managed-host-run.ts` module whose small interface owns submit, attach/status projection, cancel, worker execution and reconcile. A run gets a generated `hrun_*` identity and an immutable root under `.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`.

Submit writes immutable/spec-bound state atomically: `spec.json`, digest-only `owner.json`, 0600 one-shot `input.cap` and `input.prompt`, initial `snapshot.json`, and append-only `events.jsonl`. The hidden worker wins `claim.json` using exclusive create, validates the one-shot capability, unlinks both input files, marks `claimReady`, acquires provider admission, launches the private provider adapter and periodically advances `workerHeartbeatAt`. Provider output updates a separate `lastProviderProgressAt` only when observable; unsupported observability is represented as `unobservable`, never fabricated.

A terminal is created exclusively and exactly once. It records outcome, timing, exit/timeout/cancel reason, provider identity, spec/profile binding digests, evidence journal digest, process cleanup facts, residual process state and an independent `replacementSafe`. Repeated status/cancel/attach calls first acquire a short `reconcile.lock`, re-read facts, and materialize terminal truth for deadline expiry or authoritative worker/provider death. Silence is never a transition predicate. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity yields honest residual `unknown` and `replacementSafe:false`, not blind termination.

Initial RED tests cover: exclusive claim winner, unchanged running state across silent intervals, worker crash followed by deadline reconciliation, one terminal under concurrent reconcilers, idempotent status/cancel, terminal/result digest stability, capability/prompt deletion, and no automatic retry.

## CHK-002 — Expose submit, attach, status and cancel command surfaces

Extend the host-run command schema:
- `host_run --detach` submits, waits only for a bounded claim handshake, and returns `runId/state/deadlineAt/generation`;
- foreground `host_run` calls the same submit path then attaches to that run, projecting live output and final usage without owning the provider child;
- `host_run_status --runId ... --waitMs ...` performs bounded long-poll, returning immediately on terminal or snapshot-generation change and otherwise after at most 30000ms;
- `host_run_cancel --runId ... --reason ...` writes an idempotent cooperative request and reconciles;
- hidden `host_run_worker --runId ...` is runtime-only and never advertised as an operator workflow.

Declare command policy, process-fact level and CLI watchdog behavior for runtime continuation. A foreground caller/watchdog exit may end attachment but cannot convert the managed run to failed or cancel the worker. JSON stdout remains one machine object; text mode keeps live stream routing and concise status guidance. The handler never stores raw prompt/capability in argv or durable public artifacts.

RED starts at CLI/handler seams: detach returns after claim, status wait is capped, foreground and detached share one run/receipt shape, cancel is idempotent, unknown run is fail-closed, and caller termination leaves the run queryable.

## CHK-003 — Supervise provider processes portably and honestly

Provider adapters remain private to ManagedHostRun and preserve canonical launcher specifications. Codex uses documented `codex exec ... -`, the worker writes the prompt to stdin and closes it. Claude retains its canonical launcher contract. Agy is unavailable for ManagedHostRun because its current print launcher accepts the prompt only in argv, so managed execution refuses it before provider spawn until a stdin or protected prompt-file transport exists.

On POSIX, spawn the provider as a new process group and persist PID/PGID plus a launch fingerprint. Cancellation/deadline cleanup is TERM → bounded grace → KILL → reap → residual probe. Identity is revalidated before signals. On unsupported platforms, managed execution refuses before provider spawn with a structured unsupported-platform terminal; it does not silently degrade to child-only cleanup.

Move the first-output clock to diagnostics only. Preserve finite total timeout/deadline, bounded output projection, provider usage candidate extraction, turn-failure diagnostic, passthrough-degradation honesty and failure classification. Worker heartbeat and provider progress are distinct fields.

RED uses real local Node subprocesses for silent completion, descendant cleanup and TERM-resistant escalation, plus injected provider adapters for Codex argv/stdin closure, overflow and parsing.

## CHK-004 — Enforce shared provider admission independent of usage-ledger mode

Extract the slot registry from the ledger-gated branch into one provider-admission module. Acquisition happens before every provider spawn regardless of `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER`; usage preflight/budget/final rows remain conditional and keep existing fail-closed/append-honesty semantics. Slot ownership token, dead-PID reclaim, corrupt-meta stale backstop and token-guarded release remain unchanged.

Inventory production provider launch sites. Managed host_run and cross_host_review use ManagedHostRun admission. Direct Codex/Claude/Gemini leaves that are not managed execution are classified by the provider execution registry as `admission_only` or `adapter_only` according to their admission owner; `legacy_unmanaged` is reserved and empty by contract, and `admission_managed` is not a status. Add a source registry/contract smoke so a new direct spawn path fails review until classified.

Preserve candidate-spec per-chunk streaming, 64KiB discard-all overflow and null first-output diagnostics. RED covers ledger-off cap contention, dead/corrupt/live slot reclaim, release race, and source inventory completeness.

## CHK-005 — Route cross-host review through managed execution

Keep `cross_host_review` as profile owner. It still resolves the authoritative story worktree, captures clean HEAD/material/storyFiles facts, authorizes read-only Codex dispatch, creates the detached review snapshot, redacts environment, computes the existing policy timeout ceiling, constructs the structured-verdict prompt and validates the returned verdict schema.

Replace only its direct provider execution with internal ManagedHostRun submit+attach using profile `cross-host-verdict` and opaque bindings. The terminal receipt is included in paired host-verdict provenance. Provider nonzero/timeout/cancel/admission refusal/invalid verdict continue to yield the existing honest blocked/error decision; no raw provider stdout becomes gate evidence.

Protect configured `provider.codex`, `cross_host_review`, bounded retry and fail-closed policies with exact source/runtime regression assertions. RED captures the current direct leaf, then proves the managed path while all existing cross-host checks remain green.

## CHK-006 — Bind formal reviewer evidence to exact managed receipts

Add a versioned managed-execution binding and a two-phase provider-authored evidence protocol. The profile owner seals opaque bindings at submit: storyId, reviewRunId, lane, intended provider/transport, prompt-envelope/body/context/assembled digests, materialHash, headHash and storyFilesHash. While running, the provider reviewer writes exactly one immutable proposal into the evidence journal: pass or findings plus truthful readManifest/readLog and its registered reviewer identity. It does not call final `review_pass_set` or `finding_add`.

Successful terminal creation seals the spec digest, proposal digest and append-only journal digest. After terminal, `managed_review_evidence_import` accepts only a runId/receipt reference, reads the sealed provider-authored bytes, and imports the existing ReviewPass/Finding shape while preserving agent/lane/reviewRun/read provenance exactly. It exposes no verdict/note/finding override fields, is idempotent, and refuses non-success terminal, residual/replacement ambiguity, missing/multiple proposals or any digest mismatch. The controller may trigger import but cannot become the reviewer or reinterpret its verdict.

Register this managed receipt/composite evidence as a canonical artifact kind in shared Proof Admissibility with producer boundary, scope, REVIEW consumer, claim kind, temporal/material role, semantic field binding and canonical reason codes. Both import-time admission and the REVIEW gate must call the same shared registry/intake/evaluator; process-fact registry declares the gate semantics but is not a substitute. The gate revalidates current terminal, proposal/journal integrity, exact ReviewRun/lane/provider/prompt envelope and current material tuple instead of trusting persisted booleans.

Native-host reviewer lanes retain their existing signed ReviewRun/pass/finding path and are not falsely described as mechanically supervised by ManagedHostRun. Main/implementer/controller-authored evidence, raw CLI output, usage-ledger rows, B-1be5-style time-window matching, pre-terminal proposals and structured degraded decisions cannot upgrade to normal managed receipt assurance.

RED tests the valid provider proposal → successful terminal seal → importer → REVIEW gate path, plus forged runId/terminal/journal/proposal, stale/cross-story/cross-lane/cross-provider/material mismatch, raw CLI absence, controller override/self-assertion, multiple proposals, importer replay, and non-success terminal. Create an auto-discovered aggregate smoke so no package.json script is needed. It runs focused managed lifecycle, command, real process-group, admission, cross-host and receipt-gate tests. GC removes only terminal runs beyond retention; active runs and unconsumed one-shot inputs are protected, while failed startup cleanup removes secrets.

Update `docs/host-run-usage.md` and add `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` as the durable decision truth. Document exact operator commands, 30-second wait semantics, deadline reconciliation, no silence-based restart, the `managed`/`admission_only`/`adapter_only`/`readiness_probe` registry terms, that `legacy_unmanaged` is reserved and `admission_managed` is not a status, the local same-uid trust ceiling, and that native subagents are out of scope.

Rollout is compatibility-first for non-review agent runs but enforcement is immediate for the new managed CLI-review evidence class: a raw CLI execution may still be used manually, but it cannot satisfy a formal managed reviewer gate. Final verification includes build, focused aggregate smoke, existing host-run/cross-host/provider/dispatch/review/gate suites, process/runtime registry contracts, source scans, protected timeout diff, and a real caller-detach scenario whose original run reaches terminal without a duplicate.

  ✓ After writing / modifying code — verify before committing

  ✓ REVIEW preflight — CLI gates (--channel / --concept / --lint / docs-drift, plus conditional codex-adapter) run automatically

  ✗ No code changes since last green run — skip to save time

  lattice validate                    # standard: static + logic + integration

  lattice validate --full=PvE         # filter real machine tests by name
  lattice validate --json             # structured ExternalVerifierResult output

  1. --channel: normal channel requires implementer commits
  2. --concept: deleted symbols with ≥5 residual refs → spawn reviewer

  5. codex-adapter: required only when Codex adapter surfaces changed
  6. english-artifacts: branch commits + story metadata must be English (B-5f42)
  7. lattice-residue: scan tracked source for un-rebranded brand residue (B-292d)

EXAMPLES

  # Standard validation
  lattice validate

  # Full with real machine tests
  lattice validate --full

  # JSON output for programmatic consumption
  lattice validate --json

  # Only lint gate (quick, seconds)
  lattice validate --lint

STEP-BY-STEP
  1. Write code + tests
  2. lattice validate — fix any failures
  3. Repeat until green
  4. git commit + lattice checklist_update --status=done

    --full      string|array     Include real-machine tests (--full or --full=PvE to filter by name).

     2	
     3	Proofbound launches Codex and Claude as managed cross-provider CLI processes.
     4	`lattice host_run` submits those processes to a durable
     5	`ManagedHostRun`: the detached worker, not the caller shell, owns the provider
     6	until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
     7	return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.
     8	
     9	The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not
    10	the execution owner and disabling them does not disable shared provider-process
    11	admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions
    12	that never used the managed boundary.
    13	
    14	## Why this exists
    15	
    16	A 2026-07-10 token-burn audit found the usage ledger only ever saw a handful of
    17	probe rows: host-side reviewer launches, quorum cross-host reviews, and long
    18	desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
    19	`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive
    20	terminal receipt. The runtime persists under the primary worktree at
    21	`.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`, so Story worktree cleanup cannot erase an
    22	active run or its receipt; secrets and prompt bytes are 0600
    23	one-shot inputs removed when the worker claims them. Interactive desktop and
    24	native-subagent lifecycles remain outside this boundary and are covered only by
    25	their host or by read-only retrospective diagnostics.
    26	
    27	Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the
    28	workflow, never satisfy REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority evidence, and never advance a
    29	phase.
    30	
    31	## `host_run`
    32	
    33	```
    34	lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
    35	  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
    36	  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
    37	  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
    38	  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
    39	  [--json]
    40	```
    41	
    42	`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
    43	`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
    44	run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:
    45	
    46	```bash
    47	lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
    48	lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
    49	```
    50	
    51	`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
    52	inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
    53	only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
    54	receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
    55	never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
    56	absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
    57	touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
    58	cleanup made replacement safe.
    59	
    60	An ordinary host run executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
    61	target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
    62	the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
    63	never diverge from where the ledger says it ran. A formal `--managedReview` is
    64	different: the runtime-artifact registry resolves the canonical **primary
    65	worktree** as the durable runtime/audit root for the sealed run, output journal,
    66	terminal receipt, receipt archive, and imported evidence. A linked Story
    67	worktree may submit the run, but is not the durable runtime location and can be
    68	removed at DONE. The provider executes only in a fresh detached scratch
    69	worktree at the submitted HEAD. The scratch is read-only for Codex and is
    70	retained until terminal cleanup is proven replacement-safe; it is never a
    71	substitute for the audit root.
    72	
    73	Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
    74	caller as it arrives, up to the per-run 8 MiB retention ceiling. The foreground
    75	projection is explicitly bounded: once the ceiling is reached, `--json` reports
    76	`truncated=true` on the `lattice.host_run.v1` result and text mode writes
    77	`truncated=true` to stderr; neither promises the omitted tail.
    78	`host_run_status --json` exposes the same flag as `output.truncated`. Worker
    79	heartbeat and `lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
    80	the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
    81	only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
    82	is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
    83	is written to stderr, for example:
    84	
    85	```
    86	usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
    87	```
    88	
    89	Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
    90	usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
    91	capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
    92	flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
    93	poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
    94	happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
    95	retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
    96	usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
    97	rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
    98	valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
    99	later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
   100	(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
   101	perfectly good final usage event).
   102	
   103	### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)
   104	
   105	| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
   106	|---|---|---|---|
   107	| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
   108	| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |
   109	
   110	In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
   111	delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
   112	result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the JSON result reports
   113	`truncated=true` and does not promise the omitted tail; the JSON `stdout` field
   114	carries only the bounded usage-parse tail, not an unbounded or complete
   115	transcript.
   116	
   117	If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
   118	but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
   119	`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
   120	`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
   121	downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
   122	delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
   123	event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
   124	stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
   125	stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
   126	contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
   127	once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
   128	skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
   129	passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
   130	outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
   131	serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
   132	by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
   133	command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
   134	from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
   135	fires while a listener is attached. If the drain cap wins, one shared guard stays
   136	per physical stream until each pending write settles; its release is deferred
   137	through the next event-loop turn because Node `Writable` can invoke the write
   138	callback before emitting the same failed write's `EPIPE` event. This contains the real
   139	callback-then-error ordering without retaining one listener per foreground run.
   140	
   141	Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
   142	runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
   143	forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
   144	non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
   145	`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.
   146	
   147	### Reviewer launch
   148	
   149	Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
   150	when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
   151	registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
   152	lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
   153	identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
   154	registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
   155	in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
   156	attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
   157	process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.
   158	
   159	An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
   160	`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
   161	review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
   162	the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
   163	direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
   164	below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
   165	capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
   166	registered broker set.
   167	
   168	`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers` is an object containing a `brokers` array. Each
   169	registration has all four required fields: `brokerId` (the unique trusted broker
   170	name), `adapterId` (the adapter identity the attestation claims), `host` (exactly
   171	`"codex"` or `"claude"`), and `publicKey` (the broker's Ed25519 public key).
   172	For example:
   173	
   174	```json
   175	{
   176	  "nativeReviewInvocation": {
   177	    "brokers": [{
   178	      "brokerId": "desktop-codex-review-broker",
   179	      "adapterId": "desktop-codex-adapter-v1",
   180	      "host": "codex",
   181	      "publicKey": "<Ed25519 public key>"
   182	    }]
   183	  }
   184	}
   185	```
   186	
   187	The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
   188	ledger is replay protection, not a same-UID security boundary. Likewise process
   189	ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
   190	view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
   191	Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
   192	matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
   193	instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.
   194	
   195	Reviewer Prompt 不应由调用方手工拼接或假定某个 rollout mode。先由
   196	`review_run_start` 按当前 Story、lane 和 `promptEnvelope.roles` 的逐角色 flag
   197	选择可信正文与 full/incremental context，再让 `host_run --managedReview`
   198	按 `reviewRunId` 重新取得并校验这份内容。当前可独立启用 `lattice-review-concept`、
   199	`lattice-review-quality`、`lattice-review-test-coverage`、
   200	`lattice-review-behavior`、`lattice-review-docs`；未启用角色保持
   201	`legacy-full-context`，retired channel 不可进入该 rollout。
   202	
   203	ReviewRun 摘要会记录 rollout mode、role-body/context/assembled digest、selection
   204	reason 和预算判定。reviewer 如发现增量材料不足，必须通过既有 escalation
   205	reason 请求 full context；feature flag 本身不会授予 incremental eligibility，
   206	也不会改变 pass/finding 的签名与 freshness 门禁。在途 legacy pass 仍只按其
   207	原始 ReviewRun/round/Envelope 解释，不能因后来切换 flag 被重新绑定。

   209	For a formal managed review, the provider must remain in its host-configured
   210	detached scratch worktree. It must never `cd` to, execute commands in, or write
   211	to the canonical Story worktree named by the signed ReviewRun. The controller
   212	evaluates the canonical read-only acceptance topology, pre-review, rollout
   213	report, and rollout-policy projections before launch, then places only a
   214	bounded path-free status snapshot in the provider-visible derived prompt. A
   215	provider consumes that snapshot rather than invoking those Story CLI readers
   216	from scratch; an `unavailable` entry is an honest limitation, not permission to
   217	bypass the normal worktree cwd gate. This snapshot is provider context only: it
   218	does not replace the signed report artifacts, their lifecycle gates, or their
   219	canonical consumers. The original signed ReviewRun prompt stays unchanged as
   220	audit context, and the exact derived provider-prompt digest is sealed in the
   221	managed run before receipt import.
   222	
   223	```bash
   224	# 1. Controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
   225	lattice review_run_start '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","agent":"lattice-review-quality"}'
   226	
   227	# 2. Submit the exact provider reviewer; raw `bash + codex exec` is unmanaged.
   228	lattice host_run '{"host":"codex","storyId":"B-xxxx","agentType":"lattice-review-quality","reviewRunId":"B-xxxx:RR-001","lane":"lattice-review-quality","managedReview":true,"detach":true,"json":true}'
   229	
   230	# 3. Repeat this bounded status call. Silence does not cause replacement.
   231	lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":<generation>,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
   232	
   233	# 4. Import only after completed + replacementSafe=true + reaped=true + residualProcessGroup=false.
   234	lattice managed_review_evidence_import '{"runId":"<runId>","receiptId":"<receiptId>"}'
   235	```
   236	
   237	Inside the provider process, the managed prompt forbids `review_run_start`,
   238	`review_pass_set` and `finding_add`. Its final assistant result must be exactly
   239	one bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope containing
   240	pass-or-findings plus truthful read evidence. This protocol overrides the generic
   241	reviewer role template's normal `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` closing rules.
   242	The protected managed Codex launcher uses `codex exec --json -s read-only -C
   243	<scratch> -`, so after a successful provider exit its formal path accepts
   244	exactly one schema-valid terminal `item.completed` `agent_message` envelope.
   245	The exact standalone raw stdout envelope remains a bounded compatibility path
   246	for a non-JSON Codex transport; Claude accepts only its terminal `result` lane.
   247	Tool
   248	logs, ordinary/raw mixed stdout, arbitrary streamed output, and controller
   249	fields are ignored. The worker validates the sealed story/provider/lane/ReviewRun
   250	tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal. Missing, malformed,
   251	multiple, or oversized envelopes fail the run closed. The
   252	`pass` form requires a trimmed note of at least 10 characters and no findings
   253	(an empty findings array is equivalent to absence). The `findings` form
   254	requires at least one fully valid finding and may carry a trimmed explanatory
   255	note of at least 10 characters. Claude's provider-facing JSON schema keeps this
   256	field type-only because that transport rejects `minLength`; the local sealed
   257	envelope parser enforces the same trimmed minimum before persistence. Both the canonical final
   258	envelope and the older compatibility proposal ingress accept that diagnostic
   259	note, then discard it before the immutable evidence proposal is written, so it
   260	can never become a formal finding or evidence field. Whitespace-only notes,
   261	missing findings, malformed envelopes, and oversized provider final results
   262	fail closed. The older
   263	descriptor-authorized `managed_review_proposal_set` command remains a
   264	compatibility path, not the formal happy path; its private signing key is never
   265	placed in the prompt, argv, provider environment, or durable run artifact.
   266	Raw same-UID CLI calls, copied environment variables, stale PGIDs,
   267	terminal/reaped runs, and ambiguous/multiple run candidates fail closed.
   268	Successful terminal creation seals the proposal and journal. That state alone
   269	is not importable: the receipt must also prove `replacementSafe=true`,
   270	`processCleanup.reaped=true`, and
   271	`processCleanup.residualProcessGroup=false`. The importer accepts only
   272	`runId + receiptId`, exposes no verdict override, and preserves the provider
   273	lane/ReviewRun/provenance. Both import time and the REVIEW gate revalidate the
   274	same shared Proof Admissibility contract. Raw CLI stdout,
   275	usage rows and time-window correlations cannot satisfy this evidence class.
   276	
   277	For a managed Claude reviewer, the worker materializes the authoritative prompt
   278	as a mode-`0600` one-shot file below the provider's exact working directory at
   279	`.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/`; Claude's workspace sandbox can therefore
   280	read it without exposing prompt text in argv. Because a detached reviewer has no
   281	interactive terminal on which to approve required inspection and Lattice CLI
   282	commands, only the signed `managed_reviewer` launch profile adds Claude's
   283	`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. That same profile supplies a bounded,
   284	non-secret `--json-schema` which fixes the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun
   285	tuple and proposal vocabulary. The schema is an unavoidable CLI argument, but
   286	contains neither prompt/capability bytes nor a controller-authored conclusion.
   287	The adapter consumes only a `type=result` event with `subtype=success` and a
   288	present provider-validated `structured_output`. Every other Claude result
   289	event is ignored, including error/non-success envelopes and success events
   290	without `structured_output`. Ordinary prose, Markdown-fenced JSON, and
   291	`event.result` are never proposal inputs. Ordinary Claude `host_run` keeps its
   292	configured permission policy and has no JSON schema, while Codex keeps stdin
   293	transport. The private leaf is named by the sealed managed `runId`; the normal
   294	worker cleanup removes it when the provider settles, and terminal
   295	reconciliation/expiry repair repeats that exact run-bound removal after an
   296	abnormal worker exit. It never scans or removes sibling reviewer prompt leaves.
   297	Missing,
   298	prose-only, malformed, multiple, or oversized proposal envelopes still fail
   299	closed.

   301	`host_run_worker` is an internal continuation command. It remains dispatchable
   302	by the detached launcher but is omitted from ordinary help/catalog discovery;

   326	## Binding conventions
   327	
   328	Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:
   329	
   330	| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |
     1	# Managed cross-provider CLI execution
     2	
     3	Status: Adopted
     4	Story: B-137a
     5	Date: 2026-08-14
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	When a Claude host started Codex (or a Codex host started Claude) with raw shell
    10	execution, the caller owned the child process implicitly. A caller watchdog,
    11	terminal disconnect, or ten-minute foreground boundary could end observation
    12	without proving that the provider had failed. Treating that loss of observation
    13	as failure caused duplicate reviewer launches; treating `running` forever as
    14	proof of health caused unbounded waits. Output silence alone answers neither
    15	question.
    16	
    17	Proofbound is host-neutral. Native Codex/Claude subagent lifecycle APIs are not
    18	portable and therefore are not the execution contract. This decision covers
    19	only Proofbound-owned cross-provider CLI processes.
    20	
    21	## Decision
    22	
    23	Proofbound owns every public `host_run` and every formal cross-provider CLI
    24	reviewer launch through a durable `ManagedHostRun`. General provider workloads
    25	such as planned steps and autopilot repair keep their existing bounded adapters
    26	but share the mandatory provider-process admission registry; they do not claim
    27	durable reviewer ownership or reviewer evidence. The caller submits and
    28	observes; a detached worker owns the managed provider process until an exclusive
    29	terminal record exists.
    30	
    31	The public surface is:
    32	
    33	- `host_run`: submit, optionally attach in foreground, or return after claim
    34	  with `--detach`;
    35	- `host_run_status`: read or long-poll one run for at most 30 seconds;
    36	- `host_run_cancel`: idempotently request cancellation;
    37	- `host_run_worker`: private runtime continuation, dispatchable internally but
    38	  hidden from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
    39	- `managed_review_proposal_set`: compatibility-only provider callback for older
    40	  adapters, not the formal managed happy path;
    41	- `managed_review_evidence_import`: verdict-free exact-receipt importer.
    42	
    43	`cross_host_review` remains the policy/profile owner for paired host verdicts,
    44	but its Codex leaf executes inside ManagedHostRun and exposes the managed run
    45	and receipt in host-B provenance.
    46	
    47	## State and liveness contract
    48	
    49	The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
    50	`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
    51	status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
    52	
    53	Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
    54	
    55	- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
    56	  snapshot;
    57	- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
    58	  arrives.
    59	
    60	Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
    61	and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
    62	observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
    63	a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
    64	however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
    65	absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
    66	`timed_out` terminal state.
    67	
    68	Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
    69	hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
    70	reap and residual probing only while the original isolated leader's PID,
    71	PGID/session shape, and start fingerprint remain continuously verified. A
    72	leaderless group with surviving descendants is not authority for a negative
    73	PGID signal: it is retained as residual with `replacementSafe=false` rather
    74	than guessed away. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove there is
    75	no residual process group.
    76	
    77	## Persistence and process ownership
    78	
    79	Each run has a 0700 directory at
    80	`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
    81	primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
    82	DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
    83	bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
    84	capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
    85	Prompt and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot files; the worker
    86	validates and deletes them before provider launch. For ordinary managed runs,
    87	the capability is likewise a 0600 one-shot file. A formal
    88	`managed_reviewer`, however, creates no durable `input.cap` private-key
    89	file: its proposal-invocation private key crosses only an inherited descriptor
    90	FD to the worker, which consumes and validates it before provider launch. Only
    91	root and runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
    92	
    93	On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Formal managed Codex
    94	reviews receive the prompt through documented stdin and an observable terminal
    95	event stream (`codex exec --json -s read-only -C <scratch> -`). Only Claude launches with
    96	`launchProfile=managed_reviewer` receive a 0600 one-shot prompt file below the
    97	exact provider cwd's ignored `.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/` tree, because
    98	Claude's workspace sandbox rejects an otherwise protected OS-temp prompt outside
    99	that cwd. Ordinary Claude `host_run` launches retain their OS-temporary prompt
   100	transport (`tmpdir()`); neither prompt path puts prompt text in argv. A managed
   101	Claude leaf is bound to its sealed runId, so normal worker cleanup and
   102	post-crash terminal reconciliation remove only that exact leaf after settlement
   103	rather than scanning sibling prompts. A detached formal Claude reviewer has
   104	no approval terminal, so only the signed `managed_reviewer` profile launches it
   105	with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; ordinary Claude host runs retain
   106	their configured policy, and the strict final proposal/parser boundary is
   107	unchanged. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only in argv, so
   108	managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy exposes a stdin or
   109	protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms likewise refuse before
   110	provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup is equivalent.
   111	
   112	## Shared provider admission
   113	
   114	Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
   115	of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
   116	token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
   117	Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
   118	not process admission.
   119	
   120	A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
   121	reclaimable only after an isolated provider PGID is also confirmed absent; a
   122	dead supervisor with a live provider group still owns capacity. Corrupt/ownerless
   123	slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release checks the acquire token so a late
   124	old holder cannot delete a slot that has already been reclaimed and reassigned.
   125	
   126	Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
   127	admission. Non-provider inspection and verification probes (including
   128	readiness/version, Git/process, provenance, evidence, and lint checks) are
   129	classified separately and do not become review evidence.
   130	
   131	### Provider execution surface classification
   132	
   133	Every production provider spawn site is classified by
   134	`ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus` (`packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts`),
   135	and `packages/main/src/tasks/provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts` fails if a
   136	new spawn path appears without one:
   137	
   138	| Status | Meaning |
   139	|---|---|
   140	| `managed` | Executes through ManagedHostRun: durable run identity, supervised process group, absolute deadline, exactly one terminal receipt. |
   141	| `admission_only` | Not managed-executed, but routed through the shared provider admission boundary, so the concurrency cap and slot accounting still apply. |
   142	| `adapter_only` | A low-level adapter module whose caller owns admission; the adapter itself makes no gate claim. |
   143	| `readiness_probe` | A non-provider-workload inspection or verification subprocess, including readiness/version, Git/process, provenance, evidence, or lint checks. Never becomes review evidence. |
   144	| `legacy_unmanaged` | A provider spawn that is neither managed nor admission-routed. **Reserved, and currently empty by contract.** |
   145	
   146	`admission_managed` is not a status value: admission and managed execution are
   147	two separate properties, expressed by `admission_only` (admission without
   148	managed execution) and `managed` (both).
   149	
   150	The `legacy_unmanaged` bucket exists so an unmanaged spawn path must be declared
   151	rather than pass silently. It is asserted empty — `provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts`
   152	requires that no surface carries it — so adding one is a deliberate, reviewable
   153	act that fails the contract until justified. It is not a claim that unmanaged
   154	execution is impossible, only that none is currently admitted.
   155	
   156	## Formal managed reviewer evidence
   157	
   158	Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
   159	ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:
   160	
   161	1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
   162	2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
   163	   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
   164	   bindings.
   165	3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
   166	   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
   167	   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
   168	   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. This
   169	   protocol overrides the generic reviewer role
   170	   template's direct pass/finding closing instructions: the provider returns the
   171	   envelope only, and the managed adapter is the sole proposal writer.
   172	   The protected managed Codex launcher uses `codex exec --json -s read-only
   173	   -C <scratch> -`, so after a successful provider exit its formal path accepts
   174	   exactly one schema-valid terminal `item.completed` `agent_message` envelope.
   175	   The exact standalone raw stdout envelope remains a bounded compatibility
   176	   path for a non-JSON Codex transport; Claude accepts only successful terminal
   177	   provider-validated `structured_output` (`type=result`, `subtype=success`,
   178	   field present). Claude non-success result events, success events without
   179	   `structured_output`, and `event.result` are ignored. Claude's signed
   180	   managed-review launch supplies a bounded non-secret `--json-schema` bound
   181	   to the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple. Tool logs, ordinary or
   182	   mixed raw stdout, Claude prose or fenced JSON, and controller fields are
   183	   never proposal inputs. The worker
   184	   validates the same tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal.
   185	   Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final envelopes fail the managed
   186	   run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
   187	   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
   188	4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result, live-output and
   189	   event-journal digests plus cleanup facts.
   190	5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
   191	   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes. Import still
   192	   fails closed unless the completed receipt proves `replacementSafe=true`,
   193	   `processCleanup.reaped=true`, and
   194	   `processCleanup.residualProcessGroup=false`.
   195	6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
   196	   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
   197	7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
   198	   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
   199	   journal, prompt and material tuple.
   200	
   201	Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
   202	proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
   203	cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
   204	environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
   205	ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.
   206	
   207	The worker's reserved durable cancellation reason
   208	`absolute_deadline_exceeded` always reconciles to a `timed_out` terminal with
   209	that exact reason, even if the next observation occurs through the cancellation
   210	branch. Human/operator cancellation remains `cancelled`; both paths retain the
   211	same cleanup and replacement-safety proof.
   212	
   213	The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
   214	signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
   215	host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
   216	binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
   217	adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public
   218	key and nonce-consumption record, but exposes no issuer command and stores no
   219	broker private key. `dispatch`, `review_run_start`, inherited environment values
   220	and raw provider CLIs cannot mint this authority. The host adapter must inject
   221	the signed attestation over a dedicated descriptor for the exact CLI process;
   222	without that integration, native direct evidence is advisory-only and formal
   223	review must use the managed path.
   224	
   225	Process ancestry is secondary evidence. An unobservable process table, as in a
   226	brokered desktop sandbox, does not negate a valid broker signature. When a full
   227	ancestry is observable, any mixed distinct provider families (Claude→Codex or
   228	Codex→Claude) veto direct evidence even if the nearest ancestor matches. The
   229	one-shot local nonce ledger prevents replay but is not represented as protection
   230	against a same-UID/root attacker capable of replacing trusted configuration or
   231	instrumenting the broker.
   232	
   233	A cross-provider CLI reviewer requires a managed terminal receipt;
   234	cross-provider CLI output without that receipt is advisory-only. An explicit
   235	`degraded-single-host` fallback is local DONE assurance through host-verdict
   236	evidence, not direct or managed REVIEW evidence, and cannot borrow either
   237	reviewer authority path.
   238	
   239	## Operator guidance
   240	
   241	`lattice dispatch` prints two explicit execution modes. A native subagent uses
   242	its host lifecycle. A cross-provider CLI reviewer must use `host_run
   243	--managedReview`; raw `bash + codex/claude/agy` is advisory-only and cannot
   244	satisfy the managed evidence path.
   245	
   246	Poll the same run with `host_run_status --waitMs 30000`. Continue observing the
   247	same run across silent intervals. Cancel only on an explicit operator decision.
   248	Start a replacement only after an authoritative terminal and only when its
   249	cleanup proves replacement safety.
   250	
   251	## Retention and trust boundary
   252	
   253	`lattice doctor` reports worker liveness, provider-progress observability,
   254	deadline/cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. Explicit
   255	`doctor --repair` garbage-collects heavy terminal run directories only beyond
   256	90 days and first revalidates sealed spec, result, event-journal, proposal and
   257	evidence-binding digests, then archives the sealed receipt, evidence-binding
   258	digest, binding projection, provider-authored proposal body, and import-seal
   259	pair (evidence-binding.json + evidence-binding.seal.json) under
   260	`.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. On recover, the proposal body is
   261	re-digested against the sealed receipt's evidenceProposalDigest, the binding
   262	body is re-digested against the archive's evidenceBindingDigest, and the
   263	archived seal's schemaVersion, runId, and bindingDigest are checked the same
   264	way as the live path. Heavy live-output and result provider text are not
   265	retained. Pre-F-127 archives that lack the later capture fields refuse closed
   266	rather than reconstructing missing bodies. Any mismatch is reported as corrupt
   267	and retained for manual review. GC does not treat a receiptId match as
   268	sufficient: an incomplete leftover is atomically replaced from still-valid
   269	live artifacts, and if neither the existing archive nor the live runtime can
   270	form a complete capture, the live directory is retained. The import-time evidence-binding seal is
   271	checked before GC, and an expired cross-host run removes only its canonical
   272	temporary detached snapshot. Active or corrupt runs and
   273	runs that still contain one-shot inputs are retained fail-closed. Failed startup
   274	removes one-shot secrets immediately.
   275	
   276	The local filesystem boundary does not defend against a same-UID or root
   277	attacker. Retained output may contain sensitive provider text and must be
   278	treated accordingly.
   279	
   280	## Compatibility and non-goals
   281	
   282	- Existing finite provider timeouts, cross-host policy ceilings, bounded retry
   283	  and fail-closed classifications remain in force.
   284	- Ordinary non-review host runs remain compatible but now gain durable
   285	  ownership and shared admission.
   286	- No remote scheduler, daemon, queue or native-host subagent abstraction is
   287	  introduced.
   288	- Usage diagnostics remain non-authoritative and never become lifecycle proof.
